floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 24 is 100% register+ordering (141/141 insns) in exactly two clusters; 3 hypotheses killed, and the cluster-1 allocation flip is PROVEN reachable (a live-range extension of `i` put `src` i

Cluster 1's i/src register inversion is CLOSED as an allocation problem: exact global.c priority model measured, requirement L_i > 1.222*L_src proven unreachable (max 1.088), find_reg steering shown i

Cluster 2 is invariant under source statement order — all 24 permutations of its four independent statements measured; the residual is a sched1 INSN_PRIORITY effect, and `s8 val` read last is now posi

Permuter broke the 3-session plateau: floor 24 -> 4 (26 -> 7 differing positions). Cluster 2 fully closed by a pointer intermediate for the p[8] read plus a new statement order; cluster 1's register i

Floor held at 4; both of session 4's frontier levers killed by an EXHAUSTIVE 288/288 directed permuter enumeration, and the pre-loop residual is re-identified as an RTL emission-order problem (not a s

Forensics corrected session 5's sched1 model and built a NEW score-9 chassis whose entire residual is one i/p-walker register swap - target's pre-loop block, both bitfield clusters and every other ins

frontier.hypothesis: The whole function closes on the h1 chassis (memory/grind/func_8003504C/chassis_h1_score9.c) as soon as the loop-1 p-walker giv is allocated BEFORE the source pseudo i - the last nine positions are exactly that swap and nothing else.
frontier.mechanism: .greg on h1 ranks pseudo 73 (i) ahead of every giv pseudo (order 79 92 162 161 160 159 180 73 156 176 124 158 157 72 139 77 99 94), so i takes $a2 first and the p-walker inherits $a3. Session 4 proved this class of flip is reachable (its src-reuse lever produced target's exact dispositions on the pointer chassis), and session 4 also proved the flow-dump ratio model does NOT predict the outcome - so the ranking must be measured, not modelled. Lowering i is measured dead on this chassis (all three reuses move away), so the lever is RAISING a giv: more in-loop refs on the p-walker, or a spelling that makes the p-walker a source pseudo again while keeping both walkers strength-reduced.
frontier.next_probe: On chassis_h1_score9.c, sweep spellings that add in-loop references to the p-walker without adding instructions - e.g. read both bytes through one pointer intermediate inside loop 1 (u8 *s = (u8 *)p + i * 10; lv = table[s[0]]; tmp = s[1];), which makes the walker a SOURCE pseudo whose refs and live range can then be steered by session 4's reuse lever, and measure tmp/grind/func_8003504C/s2/probe.sh dispositions plus the position diff after each. Track the allocno ORDER, not just the score: any spelling that puts a giv (or the walker pseudo) ahead of 73 is the win.

frontier.hypothesis: The engine score is mis-ranking the two chassis: the h1 chassis at 9 is closer to a match than the floor-4 pointer chassis, because its residual is a register swap that is PROVEN reachable while the floor-4 residual is a block rotation that is PROVEN unreachable on that chassis.
frontier.mechanism: The floor-4 chassis's pre-loop block always has four class-1 source statements (p copy, src copy, base, ptr) ahead of loop.c's movables; session 5's 288/288 directed enumeration and this session's RTL dumps both confirm no spelling reorders them. The h1 chassis has exactly one class-1 statement (i = 0) and reproduces target's preheader in full. A future session should treat chassis_h1_score9.c as the working chassis and the score-4 form only as the fallback candidate.
frontier.next_probe: Before spending a session on the floor-4 chassis again, re-read this ledger entry: the only remaining question on h1 is the allocno ranking. If a spelling reaches score 0 there, candidate.c should be replaced wholesale.

frontier.hypothesis: A decomp-permuter campaign seeded on the h1 chassis is now competitive (session 5's giv-chassis campaign was not, because its base was score 18 / permuter base 495).
frontier.mechanism: Session 4 showed random search finds allocation levers of exactly this shape (the src-reuse lever came out of ws2 at 132 s) when the chassis is close. h1 is nine positions from target with no instruction-count error at all, so the permuter's metric there should be dominated by the register swap.
frontier.next_probe: Rebuild a workspace with tmp/grind/func_8003504C/s4/mkws.sh + mkbase.sh from chassis_h1_score9.c, record the permuter base score, and run a fresh-seed campaign; harvest and --stop in-session per the fresh-seed discipline. Any find that changes the loop-1 register assignment is the answer.
